hypotheses.reasoning: One message, msg-149432 at offset 598134, throws 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded at expandReferences' every time it is processed. That kills the process with code 1. Each restart picks up again at the same committed offset 598134, so it hits the same message and crashes again. That loop is the CrashLoopBackOff, and lag on events.raw keeps growing because nothing gets past this message. The upstream services (gateway, ingest-api, enrichment, db) show no errors.

v3.10.1 rolled out at 12:43, about 3 minutes before the first crash. But it processed batches without trouble at 12:44 and 12:45, and the restarts after the crash run v3.6.8 and fail on the same message. So the crash does not depend on the new build. The deploy may have written the bad message, but nothing in the logs shows that.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-149432 (offset 598134) on events.raw out of the way: send it to a dead-letter queue, or commit offset 598135 to skip it, so event-processor can catch up. Keep a copy of the payload and check it for self-referencing or very deeply nested references. Then fix expandReferences so it detects cycles and has a depth limit, and wrap per-message processing in error handling that sends bad messages to the DLQ instead of crashing the process. Find out which producer created the message.
